title: Pinyin orthography vs actual pronunciation in AISHELL-3 annotations
hypothesis: A letter-level pinyin-to-phoneme mapping mislabels a measurable share of syllable tokens: y/w spellings hide i/u/ü medials, j/q/x + u is ü, iou/uei/uen are abbreviated to iu/ui/un, apical i after z/c/s/zh/ch/sh/r is not /i/, labial + o is /uo/, and 儿化 is written as a trailing r; an explicit orthography-resolution layer can parse every one of the 1920 distinct corpus tokens with zero silent substitutions.
